3	  "body": "Linear: [NIW2-600](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-600) · **Stacked on #478** (NIW2-599, part 1b). Merge #478 first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

## What it does

"Move to" for workspaces on local folders (ADR 0033): one item, several selected, or a recording with its exports, from the active workspace to another one, keeping the item's identity and never leaving zero copies.

**The mover** (`main/workspaces/move-item.ts`)
- Moves every file an item owns today: the media, `.kaipu/<id>.json`, the thumbnail, the cursor track, the edit project (`.edit.json`, `.edit.meta.json`, `.assets/`) and the webcam track (`.webcam.mp4`).
- Same drive: a hard link to the target name, then the source's unlink. A link never replaces a file, and keeps size and mtime.
- Another drive (or no hard links, or EXDEV): a copy into the target's `.kaipu/tmp/move-<id>/`, its sha256 compared with the source's, then placed. A mismatch leaves the source untouched.
- The target record is written first: it reserves the stem (`Name (2)` on a collision), so the media never lands before its sidecar.
- Tags remap by slug. A tag the destination does not have is created there with the same name and color.
- A journal in `userData/workspace-moves/` is only a hint. At startup, and before each group, healing looks at both disks and rolls forward or back. It never deletes the only verified copy; a case it cannot prove is kept and logged.
- It refuses, changing nothing:
  - an item whose record cannot be read (`metadataIssue`);
  - a disconnected destination;
  - a destination whose tag registry cannot be trusted;
  - an item dragged out less than 10 s ago;
  - a full drive;
  - a destination that already holds the same `assetId`;
  - anything while a recording or an export runs.

**The item lock.** Session saves, renames, deletes, screenshot overwrites and moves take one lock per item. A session save queued behind a move is refused with `item-moved` and writes nothing.

**Groups.** `workspaces:move-items` runs N single moves one after another. It holds the switch lock (a new `moving` state) from the first item to the last and reports "Moving 3 of 12". A failure does not stop the rest. Stop lets the item in flight finish.

**UI** (design "Kaipu Workspaces v2", section 2)
- An "IN · Work ▾" chip at the right of the header in both editors and on the item page. Its menu shows "Belongs here", then "Move to" with each destination's cost: same drive · instant, other drive · copies, or not connected. The chip is locked, with the reason, while recording, exporting or moving.
- Moving from an editor closes it first. It goes through the same flush and leave guard as a workspace switch.
- Library: a "⋯" menu on every card and row, and a **Select** mode:
  - checkboxes, and shift-click ranges in the order on screen;
  - a bottom bar "N selected · Move to ▸" with progress and Stop.
  - Every filter stays, and changing one clears the selection. Items that fail stay selected, so a retry is one click.
- Moving a recording that has exports asks "This recording has N exports in Work. Move them too?", with **Move all N+1** or **Move only the recording**.
- The result toast lists what moved, what stayed and why, plus anything not started after Stop. It offers **Switch**.
- When no other workspace exists, the menus offer "New workspace…". It reuses part 1b's dialog and creates or adopts the folder **without switching** (`activate: false`), then moves into it.

## Where the spec and the mock disagreed (the spec won)
- Mock footnote "keeps tags that exist in the destination": the spec and ADR 0033 (decision 7) create missing tags with the same name and color. The footnote now reads "Its tags come along by name."
- Mock "only one workspace · no chevron, no menu": spec decision 19 puts "Move to ▸ New workspace…" in the editors too, so the chip always has a menu.

## Where the code amends ADR 0033 (in the ADR, dated)
- A collision takes ADR 0035's ` (2)` tail, not `<id>-2`. The moved file's name then still follows its title.
- On the same volume the move is a hard link plus unlink, because a `rename` would replace a file at the destination.
- The webcam track (ADR 0037) moves with the item. It is verified by sha256 across drives.

## Not in this PR
- **Synced folders** (decisions 4, 9 and 13). The app does not detect a synced folder yet, so those branches are not built.
- **Cloud-only items and the cloud `workspaceId` step** (part 4). A cloud-only item cannot be checked or moved, and says why.
- **A screen for quarantined moves.** They are kept in `userData/workspace-moves/` and logged at every start.
- **The drag rule in the menu.** A target is not disabled for an item dragged under 10 s ago; the move is refused with that reason instead.

## Review round (Wachiman, pullfrog, CodeRabbit)
- **Healing is stricter about what it deletes.** Rolling a committed move forward now removes the source media and files only while the source is still the moved item: its record carries the same `assetId`, the media still matches the journal, and its edit project is the one that was copied. A source that changed while the target was unplugged is quarantined and left intact; a stem that now belongs to another item is left alone. A source media that cannot be removed keeps its record and the journal, so the file is not listed again under a new identity.
- **Healing no longer empties `.kaipu/drag/`.** It also runs while the app is open, when another item's drag copy may still be read. Startup and quit already sweep it. ADR 0033 decision 11 says so now.
- A failing heal after the commit no longer turns a finished move into an "I/O" failure, and the move reports its real mode (linked or copied).
- A group move that throws reports `stale`, `maintenance` or `io` for what it was; a failed device-id read is not cached; `ensureByName` stops minting tags at the per-item cap.
- The ⋯ menu works from the keyboard: keys pressed inside it no longer open the card or row; focus moves into the menu on open and back on close; select-mode cards expose `aria-pressed`.
- Result toast: a Stop before the first move says nothing moved; exports move in on-screen order; a lost IPC reply says the result could not be read and to check both workspaces.
- Spanish strings say "espacio de trabajo".

## Checks
- `tsc` (node + web), `oxlint` (0 errors), `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- `vitest run` in `apps/kaipu-record`: 389 files and 4409 tests pass (the final push re-ran the workspace and move suites: 192 tests pass).
- New engine tests run on the real filesystem in temp folders:
  - a crash at every step, linked and copied, then healing leaves exactly one listed, intact copy;
  - the EXDEV branch;
  - a sha mismatch;
  - a collision;
  - the item lock;
  - an unreadable record;
  - tags;
  - a target disconnected while healing.
- **Not run on this machine (by rule):** Electron, Playwright and `/verify`. The app was never launched for this PR, so every UI step below is still unverified on the real app.

## How to test it yourself
Use a copy of your Library, or test items. Before you start, add a second workspace on the internal disk ("Personal").

1. **Same disk.** In the Library, open "⋯" on a recording that has tags and an edit project, then choose Move to ▸ Personal. The row says "Same drive · instant".
   - Expected: it disappears from Work. Switch to Personal: it is there with the same title, tags and edit project, and the editor opens without "missing dependencies".
   - In Finder, nothing named after the item is left in Work's folder or its `.kaipu/`.
2. **USB drive.** Add a workspace on a USB stick (Settings → Workspaces → New workspace… → Use an existing folder…). Move a large recording there. The row says "Other drive · copies".
   - Expected: the toast reports the move, and the file plays from the USB workspace.
3. **Unplugging mid-move.** Move a multi-GB recording to the USB workspace and pull the stick while it copies.
   - Expected: the toast says it stayed in Work with a reason, and the recording still plays in Work.
   - Reconnect and relaunch: exactly one copy is listed, in Work. The stick's `.kaipu/tmp/` holds no `move-…` folder.
4. **Multi-select.** In the Library, click **Select**. Click one card, then shift-click another: everything between them is checked. A cloud-only item cannot be checked.
   - Change a filter chip: the selection clears.
   - Select 5 items, then Move to ▸ Personal. The bar shows "Moving n of 5…" and the toast lists the result. Try **Stop** halfway: the item in flight finishes, and the toast counts the rest as not started.
5. **The exports question.** Export a recording twice. In the Library, move the original.
   - Expected: "This recording has 2 exports in Work. Move them too?"
   - **Move all 3** moves all three. Repeat with **Move only the recording**: the exports stay in Work.
6. **The editor chip.** Open a recording in the video editor. The header's right end shows "IN · Work ▾", and its menu shows "Belongs here" plus each destination's cost.
   - Choose Personal: the editor closes and the recording moves.
   - Start an export and open the chip again: the menu says "Wait for the export to finish" and nothing can be picked.
   - Repeat with a saved screenshot in the image editor.
7. **Keyboard.** Tab to a card's "⋯", press Enter: the menu opens and focus is on the first destination. Press Enter on it: the item moves, and the card does not open. Reopen the menu and press Escape: focus returns to "⋯".
8. **One workspace.** Remove Personal from the list. In "⋯", the only entry is "New workspace…". Create one: the item moves into it, and you stay in Work.

  "body": "Linear: [NIW2-600](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-600) · **Stacked on #478** (NIW2-599, part 1b). Merge #478 first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

## What it does

"Move to" for workspaces on local folders (ADR 0033): one item, several selected, or a recording with its exports, from the active workspace to another one, keeping the item's identity and never leaving zero copies.

**The mover** (`main/workspaces/move-item.ts`)
- Moves every file an item owns today: the media, `.kaipu/<id>.json`, the thumbnail, the cursor track, the edit project (`.edit.json`, `.edit.meta.json`, `.assets/`) and the webcam track (`.webcam.mp4`).
- Same drive: a hard link to the target name, then the source's unlink. A link never replaces a file, and keeps size and mtime.
- Another drive (or no hard links, or EXDEV): a copy into the target's `.kaipu/tmp/move-<id>/`, its sha256 compared with the source's, then placed. A mismatch leaves the source untouched.
- The target record is written first: it reserves the stem (`Name (2)` on a collision), so the media never lands before its sidecar.
- Tags remap by slug. A tag the destination does not have is created there with the same name and color.
- A journal in `userData/workspace-moves/` is only a hint. At startup, and before each group, healing looks at both disks and rolls forward or back. It never deletes the only verified copy; a case it cannot prove is kept and logged.
- It refuses, changing nothing:
  - an item whose record cannot be read (`metadataIssue`);
  - a disconnected destination;
  - a destination whose tag registry cannot be trusted;
  - an item dragged out less than 10 s ago;
  - a full drive;
  - a destination that already holds the same `assetId`;
  - anything while a recording or an export runs.

**The item lock.** Session saves, renames, deletes, screenshot overwrites and moves take one lock per item. A session save queued behind a move is refused with `item-moved` and writes nothing.

**Groups.** `workspaces:move-items` runs N single moves one after another. It holds the switch lock (a new `moving` state) from the first item to the last and reports "Moving 3 of 12". A failure does not stop the rest. Stop lets the item in flight finish.

**UI** (design "Kaipu Workspaces v2", section 2)
- An "IN · Work ▾" chip at the right of the header in both editors and on the item page. Its menu shows "Belongs here", then "Move to" with each destination's cost: same drive · instant, other drive · copies, or not connected. The chip is locked, with the reason, while recording, exporting or moving.
- Moving from an editor closes it first. It goes through the same flush and leave guard as a workspace switch.
- Library: a "⋯" menu on every card and row, and a **Select** mode:
  - checkboxes, and shift-click ranges in the order on screen;
  - a bottom bar "N selected · Move to ▸" with progress and Stop.
  - Every filter stays, and changing one clears the selection. Items that fail stay selected, so a retry is one click.
- Moving a recording that has exports asks "This recording has N exports in Work. Move them too?", with **Move all N+1** or **Move only the recording**.
- The result toast lists what moved, what stayed and why, plus anything not started after Stop. It offers **Switch**.
- When no other workspace exists, the menus offer "New workspace…". It reuses part 1b's dialog and creates or adopts the folder **without switching** (`activate: false`), then moves into it.

- Mock footnote "keeps tags that exist in the destination": the spec and ADR 0033 (decision 7) create missing tags with the same name and color. The footnote now reads "Its tags come along by name."
- Mock "only one workspace · no chevron, no menu": spec decision 19 puts "Move to ▸ New workspace…" in the editors too, so the chip always has a menu.

## Where the code amends ADR 0033 (in the ADR, dated)
- A collision takes ADR 0035's ` (2)` tail, not `<id>-2`. The moved file's name then still follows its title.
- On the same volume the move is a hard link plus unlink, because a `rename` would replace a file at the destination.
- The webcam track (ADR 0037) moves with the item. It is verified by sha256 across drives.

## Not in this PR
- **Synced folders** (decisions 4, 9 and 13). The app does not detect a synced folder yet, so those branches are not built.
- **Cloud-only items and the cloud `workspaceId` step** (part 4). A cloud-only item cannot be checked or moved, and says why.
- **A screen for quarantined moves.** They are kept in `userData/workspace-moves/` and logged at every start.
- **The drag rule in the menu.** A target is not disabled for an item dragged under 10 s ago; the move is refused with that reason instead.

## Review round (Wachiman, pullfrog, CodeRabbit)
- **Healing is stricter about what it deletes.** Rolling a committed move forward now removes the source media and files only while the source is still the moved item: its record carries the same `assetId`, the media still matches the journal, and its edit project is the one that was copied. A source that changed while the target was unplugged is quarantined and left intact; a stem that now belongs to another item is left alone. A source media that cannot be removed keeps its record and the journal, so the file is not listed again under a new identity.
- **Healing no longer empties `.kaipu/drag/`.** It also runs while the app is open, when another item's drag copy may still be read. Startup and quit already sweep it. ADR 0033 decision 11 says so now.
- A failing heal after the commit no longer turns a finished move into an "I/O" failure, and the move reports its real mode (linked or copied).
- A group move that throws reports `stale`, `maintenance` or `io` for what it was; a failed device-id read is not cached; `ensureByName` stops minting tags at the per-item cap.
- The ⋯ menu works from the keyboard: keys pressed inside it no longer open the card or row; focus moves into the menu on open and back on close; select-mode cards expose `aria-pressed`.
- Result toast: a Stop before the first move says nothing moved; exports move in on-screen order; a lost IPC reply says the result could not be read and to check both workspaces.
- Spanish strings say "espacio de trabajo".

- `tsc` (node + web), `oxlint` (0 errors), `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- `vitest run` in `apps/kaipu-record`: 389 files and 4409 tests pass (the final push re-ran the workspace and move suites: 192 tests pass).
- New engine tests run on the real filesystem in temp folders:
  - a crash at every step, linked and copied, then healing leaves exactly one listed, intact copy;
  - the EXDEV branch;
  - a sha mismatch;
  - a collision;
  - the item lock;
  - an unreadable record;
  - tags;
  - a target disconnected while healing.
- **Not run on this machine (by rule):** Electron, Playwright and `/verify`. The app was never launched for this PR, so every UI step below is still unverified on the real app.

Use a copy of your Library, or test items. Before you start, add a second workspace on the internal disk ("Personal").

1. **Same disk.** In the Library, open "⋯" on a recording that has tags and an edit project, then choose Move to ▸ Personal. The row says "Same drive · instant".

2. **USB drive.** Add a workspace on a USB stick (Settings → Workspaces → New workspace… → Use an existing folder…). Move a large recording there. The row says "Other drive · copies".
   - Expected: the toast reports the move, and the file plays from the USB workspace.
3. **Unplugging mid-move.** Move a multi-GB recording to the USB workspace and pull the stick while it copies.

   - Reconnect and relaunch: exactly one copy is listed, in Work. The stick's `.kaipu/tmp/` holds no `move-…` folder.
4. **Multi-select.** In the Library, click **Select**. Click one card, then shift-click another: everything between them is checked. A cloud-only item cannot be checked.

   - Select 5 items, then Move to ▸ Personal. The bar shows "Moving n of 5…" and the toast lists the result. Try **Stop** halfway: the item in flight finishes, and the toast counts the rest as not started.
5. **The exports question.** Export a recording twice. In the Library, move the original.
   - Expected: "This recording has 2 exports in Work. Move them too?"
   - **Move all 3** moves all three. Repeat with **Move only the recording**: the exports stay in Work.
6. **The editor chip.** Open a recording in the video editor. The header's right end shows "IN · Work ▾", and its menu shows "Belongs here" plus each destination's cost.
   - Choose Personal: the editor closes and the recording moves.
   - Start an export and open the chip again: the menu says "Wait for the export to finish" and nothing can be picked.
   - Repeat with a saved screenshot in the image editor.
7. **Keyboard.** Tab to a card's "⋯", press Enter: the menu opens and focus is on the first destination. Press Enter on it: the item moves, and the card does not open. Reopen the menu and press Escape: focus returns to "⋯".
8. **One workspace.** Remove Personal from the list. In "⋯", the only entry is "New workspace…". Create one: the item moves into it, and you stay in Work.

3	description: "Proposal: keep several workspaces (folders with Kaipu files), one active at a time and switched from the rail, so work captures never mix with personal ones; per-workspace setting overrides; synced folders; move an item between workspaces; an additive, downgrade-safe migration."
4	---

6	# Several workspaces
7	
8	> **Status: 🔵 Proposed** (2026-10-30). Design approved in conversation with the owner in
9	> three rounds; round 3 (2026-10-30) closed every open question. The spec is written; nothing is
10	> implemented. Design:
11	> [Several workspaces](/specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design/) · ADRs
12	> [0032](/architecture/decisions/0032-workspaces-identity-in-the-folder-one-active/),
13	> [0033](/architecture/decisions/0033-moving-an-item-between-workspaces/) and
14	> [0034](/architecture/decisions/0034-per-workspace-setting-overrides/) · Linear
15	> [NIW2-370](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-370). The dependencies NIW2-394 (#410) and
16	> NIW2-398 (#412) are merged.
17	>

19	> `Kaipu Record — <name>` next to the Default workspace's, or "Use an existing folder…"), editing a
20	> workspace's name and color from Settings → Workspaces, and the Default workspace in Kaipu's
21	> brand color `#F6055C`. The folder is only ever shown as text; it changes through **Change
22	> folder…**, which opens the native folder picker and _relocates_ the workspace: it points it at
23	> the folder where it now lives (moved in Finder, put in a Google Drive folder, a drive that
24	> mounts elsewhere) and never moves or copies files. It is refused for a folder that is not this
25	> workspace's (another identity, Kaipu items with no identity, an empty or plain folder, a folder
26	> already registered), and while a recording or export runs; the active workspace goes through the
27	> switch transaction.
28	>
29	> **Part 2 (NIW2-600, 🟡 In progress, stacked on #478):** "Move to" for local folders. The
30	> mover (same drive: a hard link; another drive: copy, sha256, then delete; a journal that
31	> heals a move the app died in), the "IN · Work ▾" chip in both editors and on the item page,
32	> the Library's "⋯" menu and select mode with "N selected · Move to ▸", the exports question
33	> and the result toast. Not in it: synced folders and cloud-only items (part 4). Parts 3–4
34	> (per-workspace settings, cloud) are still to build.
35	
36	## Why
37	
38	The owner records for work and for personal use. A leak of the work Library (a shared screen,
39	a folder sent to someone, a cloud listing) must never include personal captures, and the
40	reverse. Kaipu has paying customers, so the upgrade must change nothing they see and risk
41	nothing they have.
42	
43	## What it adds
44	
45	- **Workspaces**: any existing folder becomes one. Kaipu writes `.kaipu/workspace/identity.json` (id,
46	  name, color, initials) in a subfolder that no media file's sidecar can address (a customer's
47	  `workspace.png` already owns `.kaipu/workspace.json`), and a folder that already has Kaipu
48	  files is adopted.
49	- **Workspaces are visible from the first launch, even with one.** The existing library becomes
50	  a workspace named "Default workspace". The rail shows its tile and a "+" tile, the status bar
51	  shows the chip, and a one-time dismissible hint ("New: workspaces — keep work and personal
52	  captures apart") points at the rail. Menus offer "Move to ▸ New workspace…" when no other
53	  workspace exists.
54	- **One active workspace**, switched with one click on its tile in the navigation rail, and
55	  named in the status bar, the window title and the tray (captures start without the main
56	  window). ⌘1…⌘n switch while the window is focused. The Library, editors, tags and new
57	  captures use it. Switching is locked while anything is being written, and is a transaction:
58	  editors flush and close, pending toasts are dropped, and main rejects calls from the old
59	  workspace.
60	- **"Saving to Work" everywhere a capture lands**: Record page (the line "Recording to Work ·
61	  Switch" replaces "Ready to record"), control bar (hidden when the bar is in the video), capture
62	  panel and overlay, export sheet, and the toast ("Saved to Work", a label with no move control).
63	- **Settings → Workspaces** replaces Settings → Files: add, rename (name, color, initials), show
64	  in Finder, remove from list, delete (Kaipu's files to the Trash; media never touched), and
65	  "Assign to workspace…" for cloud items that belong to no workspace on this Mac.
66	- **Move to** from a new "⋯" menu on Library cards and rows, the item page and both editors. It
67	  keeps the item's identity, remaps tags by name, adds a suffix on a name collision, removes the
68	  item's drag copies from the source, serializes with the editor's saves, and survives a crash
69	  (recovery checks both media files and rolls forward; it never deletes a target because a
70	  journal says `copying`). A recording with exports in the same workspace suggests "Move all 3"
71	  or "Move only the recording".
72	- **Select mode in the Library** (it has no selection model today): checkboxes, shift-click
73	  range, and a bottom bar "N selected · Move to ▸". Moves run one after another with an
74	  aggregate progress and a per-item failure list; a failure does not stop the rest, and a
75	  group is not a transaction.
76	- **Per-workspace settings**, in the first release of workspaces: five keys (badge, upload
77	  mode, recording quality, export quality, screenshot copy) can be overridden per workspace and
78	  inherit from "All workspaces" otherwise. Shortcuts are always global. Every settings snapshot
79	  is the effective one of the active workspace, a capture keeps the policy it started with
80	  (also in the editor that opens after a failed save), and overrides in a folder this Mac did
81	  not write stay inactive until the user confirms them once ("Use them / Ignore"). With one
82	  workspace the scope selector is hidden, but a row set by an override still shows it and can
83	  reset it.
84	- **Synced folders**: a workspace may live in Google Drive, OneDrive or iCloud Drive. Kaipu
85	  labels it, keeps its scratch files outside it, always copies and verifies when a move
86	  touches it, and shows offloaded files as "In the cloud". Drawing the Library never
87	  downloads one: an evicted file or an evicted thumbnail gets no image URL, and the media
88	  protocol refuses it.
89	- **Cloud**: each cloud asset records its workspace on the server, and a Library hides the
90	  other workspaces' cloud items.
91	- **No combined Library view.** "All workspaces" exists only as the Settings scope for
92	  defaults.
93	
94	## Before implementation
95	
96	- Linear [NIW2-568](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-568), sidecar read hardening, lands
97	  first. It is hardened, not guaranteed: a read can still fail, and a failed read must never be
98	  mistaken for a missing sidecar.
99	- A short spike on the unverified File Provider behaviours listed in the spec (hard links,
100	  renames into a provider folder, offline reads of evicted files, the eviction heuristic,
101	  iCloud Desktop & Documents, conflict-copy names). A separate spike fills them in.
102	- ADR 0021 (tag sync) needs an amendment so sync is scoped per workspace before NIW2-368 is
103	  built.
104	- Server work (`cloud_asset.workspace_id` nullable, `PUT /assets/{assetId}/workspace`) should
105	  land before or with the first desktop upload, so no cloud row exists without a workspace.
106	
107	There are no open design questions: the owner's answers of 2026-10-30 are decisions 19–25 in
108	the spec.

  `workspace.png` already owns `.kaipu/workspace.json`), and a folder that already has Kaipu
  files is adopted.
- **Workspaces are visible from the first launch, even with one.** The existing library becomes
  a workspace named "Default workspace". The rail shows its tile and a "+" tile, the status bar
  shows the chip, and a one-time dismissible hint ("New: workspaces — keep work and personal
  captures apart") points at the rail. Menus offer "Move to ▸ New workspace…" when no other
  workspace exists.
- **One active workspace**, switched with one click on its tile in the navigation rail, and
  named in the status bar, the window title and the tray (captures start without the main
  window). ⌘1…⌘n switch while the window is focused. The Library, editors, tags and new
  captures use it. Switching is locked while anything is being written, and is a transaction:
  editors flush and close, pending toasts are dropped, and main rejects calls from the old
  workspace.
- **"Saving to Work" everywhere a capture lands**: Record page (the line "Recording to Work ·
  Switch" replaces "Ready to record"), control bar (hidden when the bar is in the video), capture
  panel and overlay, export sheet, and the toast ("Saved to Work", a label with no move control).
- **Settings → Workspaces** replaces Settings → Files: add, rename (name, color, initials), show
  in Finder, remove from list, delete (Kaipu's files to the Trash; media never touched), and
  "Assign to workspace…" for cloud items that belong to no workspace on this Mac.
- **Move to** from a new "⋯" menu on Library cards and rows, the item page and both editors. It
  keeps the item's identity, remaps tags by name, adds a suffix on a name collision, removes the
  item's drag copies from the source, serializes with the editor's saves, and survives a crash
  (recovery checks both media files and rolls forward; it never deletes a target because a
  journal says `copying`). A recording with exports in the same workspace suggests "Move all 3"
  or "Move only the recording".
- **Select mode in the Library** (it has no selection model today): checkboxes, shift-click
  range, and a bottom bar "N selected · Move to ▸". Moves run one after another with an
  aggregate progress and a per-item failure list; a failure does not stop the rest, and a
  group is not a transaction.
- **Per-workspace settings**, in the first release of workspaces: five keys (badge, upload
  mode, recording quality, export quality, screenshot copy) can be overridden per workspace and
  inherit from "All workspaces" otherwise. Shortcuts are always global. Every settings snapshot
  is the effective one of the active workspace, a capture keeps the policy it started with
  (also in the editor that opens after a failed save), and overrides in a folder this Mac did
  not write stay inactive until the user confirms them once ("Use them / Ignore"). With one
  workspace the scope selector is hidden, but a row set by an override still shows it and can
  reset it.
- **Synced folders**: a workspace may live in Google Drive, OneDrive or iCloud Drive. Kaipu
  labels it, keeps its scratch files outside it, always copies and verifies when a move
  touches it, and shows offloaded files as "In the cloud". Drawing the Library never
  downloads one: an evicted file or an evicted thumbnail gets no image URL, and the media
  protocol refuses it.
- **Cloud**: each cloud asset records its workspace on the server, and a Library hides the
  other workspaces' cloud items.
- **No combined Library view.** "All workspaces" exists only as the Settings scope for
  defaults.

## Before implementation

- Linear [NIW2-568](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-568), sidecar read hardening, lands
  first. It is hardened, not guaranteed: a read can still fail, and a failed read must never be
  mistaken for a missing sidecar.
- A short spike on the unverified File Provider behaviours listed in the spec (hard links,
  renames into a provider folder, offline reads of evicted files, the eviction heuristic,
  iCloud Desktop & Documents, conflict-copy names). A separate spike fills them in.
- ADR 0021 (tag sync) needs an amendment so sync is scoped per workspace before NIW2-368 is
  built.
- Server work (`cloud_asset.workspace_id` nullable, `PUT /assets/{assetId}/workspace`) should
  land before or with the first desktop upload, so no cloud row exists without a workspace.

There are no open design questions: the owner's answers of 2026-10-30 are decisions 19–25 in
the spec.

structured_output.summary: Reviewed the 8 files of part 1. No blocker or fix. The group-move busy lock now flows through activeTransactionDeps to both the switch and relocate paths, which is correct (index.ts:346-347, 363, 480; relocate.ts:24-25, 33). Findings are two docs items and one test gap, all "consider": the backlog doc (line 26) and the spec relocate row (line 1302) still say relocate is refused only while a recording or export runs, and the dialog test's refusal list has no "moving" case. Four open review threads on these files are addressed in the current code. Two open contracts remain: whether a switch can overlap the start of a move (gate.ts not read), and whether the renderer clears the lock from the list broadcast (renderer consumer not read). For the spec, I read the IPC table region in full and grepped the rest for the relocate wording, not the whole 1,300-line file.
